tools.name: create_workflow
tools.title: Create Workflow
tools.description: Start a new, empty workflow draft and return its workflow_id. Every other tool takes that id. Nothing is persisted beyond the host's store, and creating a workflow never runs anything.

name.description: Human-readable name for the workflow, e.g. "Nightly digest".

workflow_id.description: Optional explicit id. Omit to have one minted.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.title: List Workflows
tools.description: List every workflow draft this host is holding, with node and edge counts. Use it to recover a workflow_id you did not keep, before creating a duplicate.

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.title: Get Workflow
tools.description: Return one workflow's full graph — every node with its kind, config and parentId, and every edge. This is the authoring view; use export_workflow for the portable WorkflowSchema document.

tools.name: delete_workflow
tools.title: Delete Workflow
tools.description: Remove a workflow draft from this host's store. Irreversible on a store that does not version, and it deletes only the draft — nothing that was already exported or run.

tools.name: add_node
tools.title: Add Node
tools.description: Add a node of a given kind to a workflow. The kind is checked against the live registry (call list_node_kinds first — a host may have registered its own). Omitting config applies the kind's schema defaults. Pass parent_id to place the node inside a lane. Returns the created node.

node_id.description: Optional explicit node id. Omit to auto-generate.

parent_id.description: Optional lane node id — puts this node inside that lane.

config.description: Optional config. See describe_node_kind for the fields.

tools.name: remove_node
tools.title: Remove Node
tools.description: Remove a node and every edge touching it. The edges go WITH the node deliberately — leaving them would produce edges pointing at nothing, reported as a second error the author did not cause.

tools.name: configure_node
tools.title: Configure Node
tools.description: Merge config into a node, keeping the kind's other defaults. A config that does not satisfy the kind's schema is WRITTEN ANYWAY and reported as warnings — a half-configured node is a normal intermediate state when building a graph one step at a time, and refusing the write makes it impossible to get there. validate_workflow is where 'not finished' is said.

config.description: Fields to merge into the node's config.

tools.name: connect_nodes
tools.title: Connect Nodes
tools.description: Draw an edge from one node's output port to another's input port. Omit the port names to use each kind's defaults. Both nodes must already exist — connecting to a node that is not there is an error rather than a promise to create it.

source_port.description: Optional output port on the source, e.g. "true" on a branch.

target_port.description: Optional input port on the target.

tools.name: remove_edge
tools.title: Remove Edge
tools.description: Remove one edge, named either by its edge id or by the source/target pair it connects. Removing an edge never removes the nodes it joined.

edge_id.description: The edge id, if you have it.

source.description: Source node id, if naming the edge by its endpoints.

target.description: Target node id, if naming the edge by its endpoints.

tools.name: list_node_kinds
tools.title: List Node Kinds
tools.description: Every node kind this host has registered, read from the LIVE registry rather than a fixed list — so kinds the host added itself, and kinds vendored in from the marketplace, are included. Each says whether this host ADMITS it, and a refusal names the missing capability.

tools.name: describe_node_kind
tools.title: Describe Node Kind
tools.description: One kind in full — its config schema, its default config, and its input and output ports. Call this before configure_node rather than guessing field names; the fields are deliberately not on list_node_kinds, which would turn a vocabulary query into a payload nobody reads.

kind.description: The kind name, e.g. "llm_call" or the fully-qualified form.

tools.name: validate_workflow
tools.title: Validate Workflow
tools.description: Check a workflow and return every issue TAGGED by who refused it: source "schema" means the graph is malformed and editing it is the fix; source "host" means this host will not run that kind and the fix is a capability or a different kind. Collapsing the two costs you the wrong fix.

tools.name: export_workflow
tools.title: Export Workflow
tools.description: Emit the portable WorkflowSchema document — the same JSON the TypeScript, PHP and Python runtimes all read. This is what you hand to another runtime, commit to a repo, or pass to import_workflow.

tools.name: import_workflow
tools.title: Import Workflow
tools.description: Read a WorkflowSchema document into a NEW draft and return its workflow_id, plus any issues found. Import is lenient on purpose: a document referencing a kind this host has not registered still imports, with the problem reported — refusing would lose the other forty nodes to fix one.

workflow.description: A WorkflowSchema document, as export_workflow emits.

name.description: Optional name for the imported draft.

workflow_id.description: Optional explicit id for the new draft.

tools.name: run_workflow
tools.title: Run Workflow
tools.description: Execute the graph and return per-node outputs plus ok/error. This is a SMOKE TEST of wiring and routing, not a production run: it takes no executors, so nodes fall back to their kind's own behaviour and anything needing a host capability (a terminal session, an LLM client) refuses rather than acting. Refuses outright to run a graph with validation errors, because a malformed graph produces failures that look like engine bugs and are not. Seed entry nodes with initial_inputs, keyed by node id then port.
